A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. The supplied v2 ends after its references; v3 includes supplementary Sections A–E. Their contents support comparison of the documented work.

before.justification: v2 reports original Pix3D reconstruction comparisons and component ablations in Tables 1–3, alongside qualitative reconstruction results.

after.justification: v3 retains original reconstruction results and ablations, and adds an occlusion-specific evaluation and supplementary qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same joint camera/depth/mask regression, occupancy cross-attention, optional category priors, loss components and synthesis approach. The supplementary architecture, filtering and training descriptions are presented as implementation details; they do not establish a revision to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions use ShapeNetCore.v2 and Objaverse-LVIS for synthesis and evaluate on Pix3D, ObjectNet, OfficeHome and PACS. v3's occlusion breakdown subdivides images already represented in the Pix3D evaluation.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LRM and ZeroShape, each using SAM with or without pix2gestalt. v3 reuses the SAM-assisted baselines in its occlusion breakdown. The OpenLRM footnote clarifies implementation, while newly discussed probabilistic methods are not added reconstruction benchmarks.

E3.justification: v3 adds separate evaluation of non-occluded and occluded Pix3D subsets, reported as 42.6% and 57.4% of the dataset. Figure D1 also introduces a qualitative synthesis-prompt contrast. The shared mesh alignment, 10K-point sampling and CD/F-score protocol remain unchanged; Appendix B supplies previously unstated settings.

E4.justification: v3 adds the occlusion breakdown in Table 2, category-prior diagnostics for mask and occupancy regression in Figures C1–C2, and an illustration of background diversity versus silhouette adherence in Figure D1. The existing auxiliary-depth, occluder and text-prompt ablations remain, moving from v2 Table 3 to v3 Table 4.

E5.justification: Algorithm 1 newly documents random-seed generation for foreground synthesis attempts and background outpainting. This is limited seed-handling disclosure: v3 adds no fixed seed values, repeated evaluation counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged. New Table 2 reports category-agnostic FS@tau/CD of 43.6/0.082 on non-occluded images and 34.2/0.107 on occluded images, with corresponding baseline results. The headline comparison switches between previously reported model variants, not improved performance. The category-specific FS@2tau and FS@3tau entries, 66.2 and 80.4, are omitted, and supplementary qualitative results are added.

T1.justification: The feature-modulation and unprojection equations remain unchanged. Appendix B expresses the existing loss components as weighted training objectives and supplies coefficients, without adding a theorem, proof, substantive derivation or new theoretical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims retain the same scope: unified occlusion-aware reconstruction, scalable synthetic training data, strong zero-shot performance and fewer parameters. Naming the method ZeroShape-W and emphasizing the existing category-agnostic result do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the qualifications surrounding robustness and efficiency. Section 6 links smoother shapes to limited resources/resolutions and acknowledges unrealistic Copy-Paste occluders. Appendix D identifies heavy occlusion as a weakness of regression-based reconstruction, discusses probabilistic alternatives, and explains the background-diversity/silhouette-adherence conflict. The earlier boundary-clipping and dataset-ambiguity limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B supply previously missing layer specifications, ZeroShape initialization, optimizer and training schedules, loss weights, rendering and diffusion settings, IoU filtering, augmentation ranges, evaluation thresholds and mesh resolution. Hardware and training times are also documented. v3 adds a project-page pointer and identifies the OpenLRM weight source. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing changed experimental settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds works including PT43D and MeTTA, plus citations supporting implementation details, probabilistic trade-offs and ethics. Appendix D introduces a focused comparison with probabilistic reconstruction, while the main positioning against existing reconstruction and domain-randomization approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 introduces the ZeroShape-W name, updates affiliations, polishes several passages, reorganizes category-prior discussion and changes 'More Analyses' to 'Ablation Study'. Limitations gain named paragraphs and supplementary Sections A–E are appended. The main section sequence and most method exposition remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 substantially extends the visual documentation with occlusion and resource/resolution tables, pipeline pseudocode, augmentation examples, category-prior diagnostics and synthesis trade-off illustrations. Category-prior results are redistributed across tables, and ablation annotations are clarified. The original main Figures 1–9 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 refers readers to supplementary details that its supplied PDF does not contain. v3 resolves an important reproducibility deficiency through Appendices A–B, adds direct evidence about occlusion robustness, and clarifies consequential failure conditions. These gains substantially improve assessability without relying on higher headline scores. Omitting two category-specific F-score entries and their explicit VLM-overhead term is a limited loss relative to those improvements.
